How to open Lull on Windows
===========================

Lull isn't signed by a publisher Windows knows, so Windows warns you the first time.

1. Unzip Lull-windows.zip and move Lull.exe somewhere permanent, e.g. a "Lull" folder in your
   user folder or in Documents. (Launch at Login remembers where it is.)
2. Double-click Lull.exe. If you see "Windows protected your PC", click "More info", then "Run anyway".
   You only need to do this once per version.
3. If Windows asks whether Lull can use your location, allow it, so the light matches the sun where
   you are. If it doesn't ask, check Settings > Privacy & security > Location and turn on
   "Let desktop apps access your location".

Lull lives in the system tray (bottom-right, maybe under the ^ arrow). Click its icon for options.

If "Smart App Control" is on (Windows 11), it blocks unsigned apps outright and there's no
"Run anyway". In that case Lull won't run unless Smart App Control is turned off. Depending on
your Windows version that may be hard to undo, so think twice before doing it just for a wallpaper.

Needs Windows 10 (version 2004 or later) or Windows 11, 64-bit. Uses the Microsoft Edge WebView2
Runtime, which comes with Windows 11 and nearly all Windows 10 PCs; Lull offers a download link if
it's missing.

Troubleshooting: a log is kept at %LOCALAPPDATA%\Lull\lull.log and settings at
%APPDATA%\Lull\settings.json.
